name: Variance risk premium harvesting
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Monetizing Volatility Risk
caseLead: Short-dated S&P 500 index options have historically priced in larger moves than the market subsequently delivers, allowing sellers of protection to earn the variance risk premium. The premium persists because pension funds, insurers and portfolios with loss limits buy protection largely regardless of price, while few investors can absorb crash risk, and geopolitical and policy tensions sustain demand even though most events do not materially affect the index.
caseRest: The strategy typically earns small, frequent premiums but can suffer large losses when equity markets fall and volatility rises sharply. Several years of accumulated premium can be lost in a single episode because option prices and realised market moves can rise together as investors rush to reduce risk. A strong Sharpe ratio therefore overstates the safety of the return because it gives too little weight to the speed and scale of losses in stressed markets.
figNote: Each card shows the highest closing level of the VIX during the episode. The VIX measures the volatility that S&P 500 options price in for the next 30 days: it has averaged about 19 over the long run, while readings above 30 signal market stress.

events.title: Rising bond yields trigger a record VIX jump
events.text: The February 2018 volatility spike began when rising bond yields forced short-volatility products to buy back volatility, and the VIX more than doubled to a 37 close in its largest one-day rise on record. The strategy lost because short-dated option prices rose faster than the value of further-out protection.

events.title: Taiwan drills raise the cost of protection
events.text: The August 2022 rise in protection demand followed China’s largest drills around Taiwan after a US congressional visit, lifting the VIX to a 24 close. The strategy benefited because the S&P 500 barely moved, leaving realised volatility below the level priced by options.

events.title: Covid turns into a global funding crisis
events.text: The March 2020 sell-off began when a regional health emergency became a global rush for cash, lifting the VIX to an 83 close as realised volatility surged. The strategy suffered its worst loss because the market move far exceeded the protection provided by further-out options.

events.title: Ukraine invasion keeps option prices high
events.text: Russia’s February 2022 invasion of Ukraine disrupted energy and grain supplies, raising inflation and escalation risks as the VIX reached a 36 close. Results were mixed because option prices and realised volatility remained elevated for most of the year.

events.title: Bank of Japan rate rise unwinds yen trades
events.text: The August 2024 volatility spike followed a Bank of Japan rate rise that triggered an unwind of yen-funded positions, lifting the VIX to a 38 close before it fell back within two weeks. The strategy benefited because further-out protection absorbed the realised spike and volatility reversed rapidly.

events.title: US tariffs drive the largest spike since 2020
events.text: The April 2025 announcement of sweeping US tariffs drove the largest volatility spike in five years, lifting the VIX to a 52 close as uncertainty kept option prices elevated for weeks. Results were mixed because short-dated losses offset gains as realised volatility fell back.

instrument: S&P 500 index options; about one month to expiry; rolled monthly
rules: Options sold when implied volatility exceeds realised volatility; protection bought further out of the money; size reduced before central bank meetings and other scheduled events
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads and commissions deducted at each roll

marketWatch: One-month S&P 500 implied volatility is about 3.1 points above realised volatility, close to its long-run average spread. A central bank rate decision is due this week. Around past decisions, index option prices have tended to rise before the announcement and fall back afterwards.

favourable.heading: Priced geopolitical risk stays contained
favourable.text: Regional tensions favour the strategy when they raise index protection costs faster than realised S&P 500 volatility because most US earnings have little direct exposure. Tension in the Taiwan Strait or threats to Gulf shipping can therefore push implied volatility above realised volatility, creating the premium the strategy earns.

favourable.heading: Stable monetary policy guidance
favourable.text: Clear forward guidance favours the strategy because it limits realised volatility around policy meetings while short-dated options continue to price event risk. Most of 2010 to 2019 followed this pattern, as policy outcomes rarely generated the moves embedded in option prices.

favourable.heading: Volatility normalises after shocks
favourable.text: Falling realised volatility after a shock favours the strategy because implied volatility often remains elevated, restoring the gap earned on short-dated options. After the April 2025 tariff shock, this normalisation allowed premium sellers to recover much of the drawdown within months.

adverse.heading: Regional shocks spread globally
adverse.text: Regional shocks hurt the strategy when they spread into global funding markets, causing realised volatility to outrun both short-dated premiums and longer-dated protection. In March 2020, the VIX rose from about 15 to above 80 in four weeks, beyond the level covered by the protective options.

adverse.heading: Crowded positioning amplifies volatility spikes
adverse.text: Crowded short-volatility positioning hurts the strategy when higher bond yields force funds to buy back exposure together, pushing volatility beyond the level justified by economic fundamentals. In February 2018, the VIX more than doubled in a single day, so losses reflected forced buying rather than economic news.

adverse.heading: Geopolitical escalation disrupts supply
adverse.text: A prolonged supply disruption would hurt the strategy by raising inflation while reducing earnings, keeping volatility high for months rather than days and eroding repeated short-dated premiums. The stress tests below examine this scenario through a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz or Taiwan.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500, implied volatility and interest rates, which are then applied to the strategy’s current positions, including the protective options.
